location.institution: Deutsches Museum (replica; the originals are on the Moon)

object.medium: Electric vehicle: aluminium chassis, four wire-mesh wheels with individual motors, silver-zinc batteries, folding frame
object.description: The Lunar Roving Vehicle is the car the last three Apollo crews drove on the Moon. Built by Boeing with General Motors in under two years, it folded into a bay of the lunar module, weighed 210 kg on Earth and ran on silver-zinc batteries, with a motor in each wire-mesh wheel and a navigation system that always pointed the way home. Three were left on the Moon in 1971 and 1972; this is a 3D reconstruction, from scans and the original drawings, of the Deutsches Museum's replica.
facts: On Apollo 15, 16 and 17 the rovers drove a total of about 90 km, and the Apollo 17 crew went 7.6 km from their lander, the furthest humans have walked or driven from safety on another world.
The wheels are woven from zinc-coated piano wire with titanium chevrons for tread, so they would not clog with dust or crack in the cold.
Gene Cernan set the lunar speed record of 18 km/h in the Apollo 17 rover, and its television camera filmed the lunar module's launch.
